title: Isolate Terraform networking graph and introduce explicit contract modules
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our networking Terraform surface has accreted implicit coupling between VPC blueprints, shared IAM artifacts, and environment overlays which makes incremental upgrades (provider bumps, region sharding, and NAT behavior tuning) risky and slow. Several teams have worked around these edges by shadow modules and ad-hoc outputs, increasing plan time and cross-stack drift.

Goal: Decompose the monolithic networking modules into a small set of explicit contract modules (vpc-core, vpc-egress, subnet-primitives, routing-contracts) with clear inputs/outputs, remove cross-cutting outputs that create dependency cycles, and add a migration harness and CI checks to validate idempotency across workspaces. This refactor should enable safe aws/gcp provider upgrades and reduce plan/churn for ephemeral envs.
acceptance_criteria:
- vpc-core and subnet-primitives are implemented and documented with typed inputs.
- No Terraform cycles between iam/networking/resource groups across staging and production overlays.
- End-to-end test runs (plan+apply+destroy) in a sandbox workspace complete with no diffs for pinned example env (dev-labs) after migration.
- Provider upgrade from aws v4.x -> v5.x can be performed in a canary workspace without manual state surgery.
- CI gate enforces: module lint, tfsec, plan-time < 60s for core changes in sandbox projects.
implementation_plan:
1) Audit current module graph using terraform graph + custom parser to surface hidden outputs and cross-workspace refs.
2) Draft new module interfaces (vpc-core, vpc-egress, subnet-primitives, routing-contracts) and publish RFC to infra-modernization channel for review.
3) Implement modules in a separate branch and add unit examples in /examples/dev-labs.
4) Add migration scripts that map old outputs to new inputs and an automated tfstate import helper for one-off resources.
5) Run staged migration: sandbox -> staging-> production canary (single region) and validate plans.
6) Deprecate legacy overlay usage, update docs, and create a follow-up ticket to remove legacy modules after 30 days.
migration_steps:
- Step 0: Create backup snapshots of current tfstate and export to S3 with retention.
- Step 1: Deploy vpc-core in parallel for canary environment using new module interface (no destroy of old infra).
- Step 2: Use migration helper to copy outputs that are consumed by downstream overlays to new stable outputs, and run terraform refresh+plan to verify no drift.
- Step 3: Swap overlay references in canary workspace to new module outputs, apply and validate.
- Step 4: Repeat for other environments; monitor metrics (plan time, number of resources changed) and roll forward.
- Step 5: Remove legacy module references and run full import tests.
testing_plan:
- Add integration example under examples/dev-labs with a GitHub Actions workflow: terraform init -> validate -> plan -> apply -> run smoke tests -> destroy.
- Add unit test harness for module interface using terratest (Go) and a lightweight AWS emulation for negative tests.
- CI rules: any change touching modules/networking/ requires a successful plan in sandbox before merging; plan output must be reviewed by infra owner.
rollback_plan:
If a migration causes unexpected diffs or a service regression:
- Stop rollout and re-point overlays to the previous module outputs (we keep old outputs for 7 days after migration).
- Restore tfstate snapshot from S3 and apply to reconcile any accidental drift.
- Revert the merge and create an incident postmortem capturing root cause and required follow-ups.
